eye_of_the_horizon.title: The Eye
texts: Final entry in this series. A captive black hole wrapped in anchors, lenses and stabilisers - used as a computer. It simulates stars, galaxies, universes, and keeps what falls out.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.
Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why a black hole? By the $(thing)Bekenstein bound$(), a horizon holds the most information any region of space can. Bekenstein and Hawking showed its entropy scales with horizon area, not volume. If anything can hold a universe in memory, it is this.

Three simulations, each gated by coil tier:$(li)a $(thing)stellar life cycle$() (tier 4)$(li)a $(thing)galaxy$() (tier 5)$(li)a whole $(thing)cosmology$() (tier 5)$(br2)Each run returns a huge spread of materials - and $(item)Horizon Shards$().
Last note on throughput: field emitter tiers multiply its parallels, just like every other multiblock. I keep looking into the lens and feeling it look back.
Day 1 of the singularity work. The $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() focuses so much light into one point that it collapses into a black hole.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

A $(thing)kugelblitz$() (German: 'ball lightning') is a real prediction of general relativity: energy curves spacetime just as mass does, so enough light in a small enough volume forms a horizon. Nobody has made one. The required intensity is absurd. Apparently, not here.

Lesson learned the hard way: while running, the singularity at its heart bends light around it ($(thing)gravitational lensing$()) and pulls in loose items and creatures. My spare tools are gone. Keep your distance.

Observation log. A running singularity bends light around its horizon: the room behind it is smeared into an $(thing)Einstein ring$(), with a bright $(thing)photon ring$() at the edge of the shadow.$(br2)White holes do the opposite.

The physics: mass curves spacetime and light follows the curve. A source directly behind the hole reaches me from every side - the ring. At 1.5 Schwarzschild radii photons can orbit; that is the photon ring, the same feature the Event Horizon Telescope imaged in M87*.
Practical note: if this conflicts with a shader pack, it can be disabled in the client config ($(thing)gravitationalLensing$()). The universe will still be curved; you just won't see it.
Extracts the rotational energy of a spinning black hole via the $(thing)Penrose process$(). My first real power from a singularity.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Penrose, 1969: around a rotating hole lies the $(thing)ergosphere$(), where spacetime itself is dragged so hard nothing can stand still. Split a particle there, drop one half onto a negative-energy orbit, and the other escapes with more energy than you sent in. The hole spins down to pay for it.
Running figures: a $(item)Micro Singularity$() burns for twenty minutes at 65,536 FE/t. Energy leaves through the controller and any $(item)Interface Port$().
A black hole, run backwards in time. Nothing can enter; everything comes out. The $(item)White Hole Emitter$() should not work. It does.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Theory check: the equations of general relativity are time-symmetric, so every black hole solution has a reversed twin - a $(thing)white hole$(), a horizon that can only be left, never crossed inward. None has ever been observed. Its lensing ring, I note, behaves the opposite way to a black hole's.
